source_title: Sonam Wangchuk Backs Women's Stir Against Liquor Policy, Slams Talks Cancellation - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Returning to Leh, climate activist Sonam Wangchuk met women who have been staging a sit-in protest for a week against the spread of alcohol and the issuance of bar licences in Ladakh. Wangchuk praised the sustainable design of the new Leh airport terminal before hitting out at the local administration for disregarding local sentiments. He questioned why alcohol is being promoted in Ladakh while Gujarat remains a dry state, pointing out that women abandoned household duties to protest in the cold. Addressing an official notice cautioning him over his statements, Wangchuk defended the demonstrators, noting past marches and press briefings. He criticised the cancellation of scheduled talks in New Delhi regarding Ladakh's demands for statehood, Sixth Schedule protections, and a legislature, expressing concern over powerless hill councils and ecological destruction along the Indus River. INDIA Bloc Ramlila Rally: Capacity Row, CTI Warns Of Rs 10k Cr Loss
Preparations are underway at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for the INDIA bloc's mega rally scheduled for November 1. While the Congress expects a gathering of ten lakh people from allied parties, questions remain over crowd management as the 12-acre venue has a capacity of only 50,000. Meanwhile, the Chamber of Trade and Industry has demanded the postponement of the rally until after Diwali, warning that disruptions across 22 surrounding markets could cause business losses of approximately 10,000 crore rupees on a peak shopping Sunday. Congress responded by citing previous political marches in commercial areas, confirming the event will proceed as scheduled.
700 Stubble Burning Cases in Punjab: Farm Fires Continue in Sangrur, Air Pollution Reaches Delhi
Over 700 cases of stubble burning have been recorded across Punjab, with plumes of smoke rising from agricultural fields in districts like Tarn Taran, Amritsar, and Sangrur. Despite government crackdowns, appeals, and the distribution of farm machinery, marginal farmers continue to set crop residue ablaze, stating they lack adequate equipment and alternative options. While overall incidents have reportedly declined, the ongoing farm fires continue to generate severe air pollution affecting Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi. Aam Aadmi Party leaders have questioned the extent of transboundary smoke reaching the capital, but ground realities confirm active stubble burning hotspots persist across the state.
UP Hikes Kanya Sumangala Aid To Rs 25,000 Across 6 Stages: Check Eligibility
Under the Uttar Pradesh government's Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana, financial assistance provided to girl children from birth through higher education has been increased from 15,000 rupees to 25,000 rupees starting financial year 2024-2025. The revised assistance is disbursed across six stages: 5,000 rupees at birth, 2,000 rupees upon completing full vaccination, 3,000 rupees each upon admission to class one and class six, 5,000 rupees on admission to class nine, and 7,000 rupees on admission to a diploma or graduation course after class 12. To qualify, families must reside in Uttar Pradesh with an annual income below three lakh rupees. The benefit covers up to two daughters per family, with an exception allowing a third daughter if twins are born in a second delivery.
JP Nadda Slams Mallikarjun Kharge Over PM Modi Remark at Health Wealth Summit
Speaking at the India Today Health Wealth Summit, Union Health Minister JP Nadda strongly criticised Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge over his controversial remark regarding Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Nadda stated that he felt ashamed of the language used by the Congress chief and condemned the party for justifying it, calling the stance a reflection of mental bankruptcy. He asserted that the country is progressing under Prime Minister Modi's leadership and suggested the opposition take lessons from the BJP on functioning constructively. The political row erupted following Kharge's heated remarks at an event in Patna.
